problem: Open-vocabulary ObjectNav methods either rely on training-free LLM/VLM prompting (costly, ungrounded, unstable) or on end-to-end RL with CLIP (sample-inefficient, poor generalization). Supervised map-based goal-prediction networks (PEANUT) are efficient but restricted to a closed set of goal categories.
motivation: Semantic-map goal prediction trains efficiently with supervised learning but cannot handle unseen goals. VLMaps-style dense CLIP maps localize objects precisely but do not encode spatial relations for finding unmapped objects, and storing dense CLIP maps for training is prohibitively expensive (about 1000x storage, 20x training time). Since CLIP text and pixel embeddings are aligned, training on cheap text-embedded maps might transfer to visual maps at test time.
key_idea: Train a goal-conditioned map-based exploration policy only on text-CLIP-embedded semantic maps built from ground-truth layout, then swap in dense-CLIP (LSeg) visual pixel-feature maps and image or text goals at inference (Cross-Modal Transfer on Semantic Mapping).
insight: Because dense CLIP features are aligned with text embeddings, a policy trained only on text-based maps of 86-100 categories generalizes to unseen goal objects and to visual maps. Vision-based inference (60.6 SR) even beats GT text-map inference (59.6 SR), which the authors attribute to feature noise reducing overfitting and to robustness against detection errors. Ablations show higher map resolution helps (45x45 beats 20x20 by 3.8 SR), and LSeg beats MaskCLIP slightly (59.4 vs 58.9 SR).
method: Language-based semantic map (training): a categorical semantic map with N channels built from HM3DSem GT (92 categories), turned into a C-dim map by a confidence-weighted average of CLIP text embeddings per cell (background as 'other').
Vision-based semantic map (inference): LSeg dense pixel embeddings are back-projected using depth and pose to a top-down map, with a running mean over observations per cell (count map N).

Goal-conditioned map encoder: patch-embed the map (16x16 patches, 45x45 tokens) plus learnable positional embedding, then FiLM conditioned on the CLIP text/image goal embedding (d=512 reduced to 64), then a 2-layer transformer with 8 heads.

Goal location decoder: one conv layer plus two transposed convs output an MxM goal probability map, trained with BCE. The long-term goal is the argmax of the probability weighted by an exponential geodesic-distance term (as in PEANUT).
Analytical local planner: FMM shortest path to the long-term goal, executing discrete actions.

Training data: goal-agnostic agent explores HM3DSem scenes for 500 steps, saving maps every 25 steps and keeping the first half. Goal objects are excluded from training (86 objects excluding the 6 goals for ObjectNav, 100 train objects for OVON). Augmentation: random crop to 720x720, flip, rotation.
Goal detection is handled by separate open-source detectors (PEANUT, L3MVN or InstructNav detection modules) for fair comparison.

setting.backbone: CLIP text encoder + LSeg (dense CLIP) frozen; small FiLM + 2-layer transformer + conv decoder trained with supervised learning
setting.model_size: small (2-layer transformer, hidden 512; FiLM dim 64); not otherwise reported
setting.training_data: Text-embedded semantic maps from HM3DSem (216 scenes, 92 curated categories, goal objects excluded); maps saved every 25 steps over 500-step random exploration; 20 epochs, ~20 h on 8 V100
setting.action_space: discrete (move_forward, turn_left/right, look_up/down, stop) via FMM planner to predicted long-term goal
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT semantic layout used only for training maps; a GT-text-map ablation exists)

results: OVExp gets 59.7 SR / 28.8 SPL on HM3D-ObjectNav with the goal categories unseen in training, close to the closed-set 60.6/29.7, and beats L3MVN by +8.5 SR with the same detector. It has lower SR than InstructNav (GPT-4, 58.5 SR) only in that setting under the same detector (56.3 vs 58.5) but a higher SPL of 27.9 vs 20.9. On HM3D-OVON val-unseen it reaches 37.8 SR against VLFM's 35.2, and beats RL/DAgger baselines (best 18.6 SR).
limitations: Trained on text-only maps of a limited object set; the policy is category-oriented and inefficient for instance image goals (lower SPL than Mod-IIN)
Training with high-resolution dense maps is expensive, so map resolution is limited (45x45 tokens); reliance on separate goal detectors and on GT semantic annotations for training
Real-world evaluation is only qualitative (demo video, Turtlebot4 with a remote server)
